utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case number IT-08-91-PT, The Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And I welcome the Office of the Prosecutor, Defence counsel, and one of the two accused. It's Zupljanin, as the other accused Mico Stanisic is on provisional release. Can the accused hear the proceedings? Can the accused hear the proceedings in a language he understands? Is there a problem? THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: You're not receiving interpretation. Oh. Is it okay now? THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] I cannot hear the interpreters, and that's where the problem lies. I can hear them now. I couldn't hear them before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Let me know if there is any further problems. But may we then proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the accused's microphone please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it okay now? THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] Yes, it is. I can hear it well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. We then proceed to the appearances. May I have the appearances first for the Office of the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Joanna Korner, Matthew Olmsted, and Gramsci Di Fazio, assisted by case manager Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, good afternoon to my learned friends from the Prosecution. My name is Slobodan Cvijetic. I'm a co-counsel in the Defence team of the accused Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Igor Pantelic, co-counsel for Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. The reasons for this Status Conference is that it is been now 120 days since the last time there was a Status Conference on 20 November 2008, administered by Judge Prost. And the parties are well aware, also the accused, of the purpose of the Status Conferences. As for the Status Conference here today, I just want to, already at this stage, mention that both parties have an interest in -- for different reasons, that, if possible we should deal with the Status Conference, of course, deal with all necessary business, but, if possible, adjourn within half an hour, approximately. I would also like to mention what has -- or reiterate what has already been communicated to the parties. That it is still the intention of this Tribunal to have all necessary preparations pre-trial stage-wise done so that the possibility is there to start the trial before the summer recess. So there is nothing new -- there is nothing new with a view to that intention already communicated to the parties. For the pending motions, I am informed that from the 65 ter conference that was held this morning, a detailed -- a detailed mentioning of all pending motions were gone through with the parties. I will briefly dwell on a few of these, but I see no need to repeat or go over again in detail with the parties those pending motions. I will mention that there -- there is now a filed decision on the form of the indictment, that was yesterday, so 19 March, and in conformity with what the Defence have requested earlier, they will now have two weeks' limit in which to comment on the motion from the Prosecution on amendments of the indictment. I should point out that it is the first motion of 1st December 2008 that is the main focus here, because the second motion, supplementary motion of 2nd March, 2009, the Defence have already commented upon. So it's basically, as I see it, the motion of 1st December 2008 and some of these issues also had an aspect or a side to issues that were dealt with in the decision now filed on the form of the indictment. So it would follow, then, that by 2nd April there should be submissions from Defence on the Prosecution motion to amend the indictment. As for Rule 92 bis, 92 ter, and 92 quater. 94 bis further judicial notice of adjudicated facts, further Rule 65 ter witness and exhibit lists, and access to materials in other cases, I rely on the 65 ter conference. And if the parties have matters within what I have already now mentioned they want to raise also here, please do so. But if not, I will just proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just this. Your Honour I assume is referring to the responses on behalf of Zupljanin, that they were not proposing to reply until there had been a ruling on the form of the indictment. So that we understand it, they have been given 14 days now to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour, just for clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: The same approach, I would suggest to follow as for disclosure, I have also here been given a briefing by the Senior Legal Officer after the 65 ter conference, so I'm well aware of the points raised there, and I rely on the parties to have contact, to -- directly between themselves, to deal with the questions that were mentioned in the 65 ter conference. The parties will remember that on the last Status Conference on 20 November 2008, Judge Prost raised the issue of agreed facts, whether it would be -- that it would be desirable that the parties continue their efforts with a view to presenting further agreed facts. I will only reiterate this now, at this stage. As far as I'm -- as far as I'm briefed now, there is no new development as yet, in the form of further agreed facts, but the Trial Chamber will still ask the parties to see if this is a possibility to further advance on agreed facts. Are there any other issues that the parties would like to raise? Naturally, I will give the floor to the accused towards the end of the Status Conference, with a view to detention and matters like that. But would there be any other matters before we go to that stage of the Status Conference?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I quite agree with what has been said so for. We had a constructive meeting at the 65 ter conference. We agreed to deal with all of the problems you have been informed of through various discussions, save for the saying that the door should never remain shut if we are to keep channels open. There's nothing much for me to add. We shall continue discussing further disclosure of evidence and related issues. I have nothing to inform you in addition to what was discussed this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just a minor intervention to the transcript, page 2, line 17, instead of co-counsel for Mico Stanisic it should be co-counsel for Zupljanin. Not a big deal. At this stage I have nothing to add, maybe depending off our time-frame today, I will raise one minor issue, but it is not so of big importance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. The condition of the accused, first, with a view to Stanisic that is currently on provisional release, is there information from counsel concerning his health? I would like to give the floor to counsel for Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Stanisic, is in good mental and physical health, and he enjoys being free. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. That brings me, Mr. Zupljanin, to you. And first I would like to hear also from you on, who are in detention, if there are matters directly related to the detention that you would like to raise. THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] Concerning detention, Judge Stole, I wouldn't say anything special. You know well what life in detention unit is like. I'm more concerned with the issue of my Defence, and this is why I believe it is necessary for me to say a couple of sentences concerning my Defence. And, of course, within the limitations of time today, because of this mass or service that I'm going to attend. Of course, my Defence will reflect heavily upon this case. My Defence team is still cutting their milk teeth, and it will take them time to be -- fall on their feet, and I have been in detention for ten months. As early as on the 13th February, I demanded that my counsel be removed. The secretariat did not or Registry did not agree. Then I filed a motion to reconsider, and I'm still awaiting for a reply. Both you and I are facing problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Mr. Zupljanin, I would like to state at this stage, I will not prevent you from briefly mentioning the issue of your legal representation. However, I am aware that there has been a decision by the Registrar and that review by the President is being asked or has been requested so that the position as of today is that this issue is before the President of this Tribunal. It is not before the Trial Chamber, at least not at the moment. It may or may not be before the Trial Chamber later, but not today certainly. So with that in mind, I would -- I would ask you to make these submissions relatively short. THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] I'll try to be as brief as possible. I said this to inform the Bench at today's Status Conference, but I will continue. I see we, both you and I, are in grave problems in my opinion. The beginning of the trial is not even on the horizon, although you said that will come before -- before the summer break. We need 24-hour/7 work to start preparing our Defence, and I have been charged with offences which certain my whole life being spent in prison, and I am innocent. Mr. Stanisic has been preparing his Defence for the fifth year running since he was in detention, and three fourths of that time he spent outside detention. So let's cut a long story short, I would like to propose to this Bench the only thing that is viable in this situation, and that is for the purpose of intensive preparations for my Defence that I be put on provisional release so that I'll be in the same status as Mr. Stanisic and I could focus on preparing my defence. Otherwise, I deeply believe that there will be no mention of a trial during this year, if I am to face a fair trial. If the intendency [as interpreted] of my Defence work continues at the same pace, I don't believe that the next year either we'll see the beginning of my trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zupljanin. It is it, of course, open to any accused and detained accused in this Tribunal to request for provisional release. That is it open to you at any given time. As now -- as of now, there is no such request or has not been such a request before us. You may want to, I take it, discuss this with your Defence, and then, if that is your wish, make such requests in the proper channels, in the proper way before the Trial Chamber. THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: If there would be, then, no other business during this Status Conference, we'll adjourn.
